audits.title: PWE-012 Audit Of Nhs Tayside Colonoscopy Surveillance Programme
audits.standard: BSG guidelines for colorectal cancer screening and surveillance
audits.setting: NHS Tayside colonoscopy surveillance programme, Ninewells Hospital, Dundee

cycle1.result: 319 requests adhered to guidelines (73.5%); 328 (75.6%) scoped; 44 colonoscopies fell outside guidelines, 38 of them brought back too early or late.

audits.other_findings: 58% of surveillance colonoscopies were normal and 1% showed cancer, with the highest normal rate in genetic family history patients. Nurse specialist review saved many appointments.
audits.citation: Elliott K, Gray L, Groome M, Rodger J, Mowat C. PWE-012 Audit Of Nhs Tayside Colonoscopy Surveillance Programme. Gut. 2014;63(Suppl 1):A126.2-A126. doi:10.1136/gutjnl-2014-307263.272.

audits.title: Surveillance colonoscopies for colorectal polyps--too often, too many! An Audit at a Large District General Hospital.
audits.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines for adenoma surveillance
audits.setting: Colorectal department, Mayday University Hospital, Croydon (large district general hospital)
audits.intervention: BSG guidelines printed, laminated and displayed in colorectal clinics.
audits.other_findings: Of 533 of 1800 waiting list notes reviewed, 17.7% met guidelines, 23.4% needed no further surveillance and 58.9% were booked earlier than recommended.
audits.citation: John BJ, Irukulla S, Pilgrim G, Swift I, Abulafi AM. Surveillance colonoscopies for colorectal polyps--too often, too many! An Audit at a Large District General Hospital. Colorectal Dis. 2008;10(9):898-900. doi:10.1111/j.1463-1318.2008.01516.x. PMID: 19037930.

audits.title: The impact of national guidelines on the waiting list for colonoscopy: a quantitative clinical audit.
audits.setting: Kent and Medway Cancer Network: seven hospitals across four NHS trusts

cycle1.result: Around 22% (n = 664) of surveillance referrals were in line with guidelines, 51% (n = 1540) could be cancelled and 27% (n = 816) could be given a new date. Average wait for diagnostic colonoscopy 76.8 days.

audits.intervention: Non-compliant surveillance referrals adjusted (cancelled or re-dated) to match the guidelines

cycle2.result: Average wait for diagnostic colonoscopy fell from 76.8 to 56.0 days (P = 0.0022).

audits.other_findings: Described as a five-stage audit cycle; the action prompted debate on social, moral and ethical issues.
audits.citation: Chivers K, Basnyat P, Taffinder N. The impact of national guidelines on the waiting list for colonoscopy: a quantitative clinical audit. Colorectal Dis. 2010;12(7):632-639. doi:10.1111/j.1463-1318.2009.01871.x. PMID: 19486094.

audits.title: Post-polypectomy surveillance documentation and guideline concordance: A retrospective clinical audit of physician documentation at a tertiary Saudi hospital.
audits.setting: King Saud University Medical City, tertiary hospital

cycle1.result: 74.9% had no documented surveillance plan; 29 (14.0% overall) guideline-concordant

audits.other_findings: 20 (9.7%) over-surveyed and 3 (1.4%) under-surveyed; most plans documented by gastroenterologists (45/52).
audits.citation: Mubarak MF, Alabduljabbar MA, Almousa MS, Ghesheyan AYH, Alkanhal IM, AlSubaie SK, et al.. Post-polypectomy surveillance documentation and guideline concordance: A retrospective clinical audit of physician documentation at a tertiary Saudi hospital. J Taibah Univ Med Sci. 2026;21(5):865-872. doi:10.1016/j.jtumed.2026.07.011. PMID: 42604010.

audits.title: Concordance of surveillance colonoscopy recommended intervals with Australian guidelines: a clinical audit in six Victorian public hospitals.
audits.standard: 2018 Australian Cancer Council surveillance colonoscopy guidelines
audits.setting: Three metropolitan and three rural public hospitals, Victoria

cycle1.result: 25.4% (63/248) of recommended intervals were guideline-concordant; of discordant, 74.6% early, 20.5% not indicated, 4.9% late.

audits.other_findings: Concordance was 0.0% (0/84) for guideline 10-year intervals and 31.0% for 3-year intervals.
audits.citation: Foo J, Joseph C, Gorelik A, Hensher M, Hiscock H, Hutchinson A, et al.. Concordance of surveillance colonoscopy recommended intervals with Australian guidelines: a clinical audit in six Victorian public hospitals. Aust Health Rev. 2026;50(3):AH26018. doi:10.1071/ah26018. PMID: 42656090.
